title: Issue 4934 fix campaign
heading: Issue #4934 fix (head b87d20dd81, rebased onto PR #4901 at 6b081187e1) against PR #4901 and PR #4898, 2026-10-15 round 2
short: Short version. With the AMX kill switch, the fix brings PR 4's prefill time back to PR 3's in every cell, and its decode throughput back to PR 3's at prompt 8192 and at tp4; at tp2 prompt 1024 it stays 1.1 % below PR 3 (the row-major tail rows scored one at a time). With AMX on, the fix is inside the band or better than PR 4 in every cell. Under FPGA attention the fix equals PR 4 at tp2 and tp4; the earlier tp4 gap was an arm-order effect.

groups.name: Kill switch (TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1), CPU attention
groups.intro: Every arm runs the same binary family with the AMX kernels switched off at run time, so the software scoring loop, the K store and the conversion are what differ. The question: does the fix bring PR 4 back to PR 3?
groups.headline: fixoff

groups.name: AMX on, CPU attention
groups.intro: The same binaries with the AMX kernels on. The question: does the fix cost anything against PR 4 where the AMX kernel scores the dense pages?
groups.headline: fix

groups.name: FPGA attention
groups.intro: Hardware attention: the FPGA scores the DMA-complete pages and the CPU scores the tail. The row-major policy of PR 4 under hardware attention is unchanged; the question is whether the fix keeps PR 4's level.
groups.headline: fix

groups.name: Ablation probes of the fix under the kill switch (commits 1 to 6, c30a86f252), CPU attention
groups.intro: Two timing-only builds of the fix split its remaining kill-switch loss. probe a1 sends every live token to the reader (no dotter path, the per-page mask read kept). probe a2 also replaces the per-page mask read by a constant. Their generated tokens are wrong, so only their timing counts. fix minus a1 = the dotter path; a1 minus a2 = the per-page mask read; a2 minus PR 3 = everything outside the loop's split.
groups.headline: fixoff

notes: Head measured: b87d20dd81 (the issue #4934 branch rebased onto PR #4901 at 6b081187e1, 7 commits), binaries verified by sha256 and version line in rt-results.txt. 3 repetitions per cell, the arm order rotated per repetition (campaign-rot.sh), 0 runs excluded.

Decision rule: (1) fixoff vs headoff inside the band in TPS and TTFT in every CPU cell; (2) fix vs new inside or better in TPS with AMX on; (3) fix vs new inside under FPGA attention. Result: (1) fails at tp2 prompt 1024 in TPS (-0.84 TPS, -1.1 %, t -8.0; band 0.40) and holds elsewhere; (2) and (3) hold. The goal of issue #4934 is not fully met, so the branch is not pushed.

Round 1 (head c30a86f252, commits 1 to 6) showed -1.7 % at tp2 prompt 1024 and -1.5 % at prompt 8192. Commit 7 (the block mask in the page's first cache line) removed the per-page mask read's cold cache line: -1.1 % and -0.8 % now. The remainder at prompt 1024 matches the ablation's dotter-path share (1.2 %): the up to 15 row-major tail rows of each user's current block are scored one row at a time, a fixed cost per step that shows at short prompts only.
The ablation group (fourth row group) is round 1's data at c30a86f252: it is the decomposition that predicted round 2, not a measurement of this head.

Traces of this head (results/i4934-r2, newoff vs fixoff, one trace per arm): decode step 14.435 vs 14.195 ms at prompt 1024 (-1.7 %), 66.985 vs 65.140 ms at prompt 8192 (-2.8 %); convert_k_blocks 1,038 us serial vs 62 us on the pool; the slowest attention worker -2.2 % and -2.0 %.
words: tron is the inference program under test. runtron is its command-line tool, which ran every cell here.

AMX is the Intel tile instruction set the stack's attention kernel uses. TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 (the kill switch) turns the AMX kernels off at run time; the AVX-512 reader and the row-major dotter score the keys instead.
PR 3, PR 4, fix; head, new, fix and their off arms

PR 3 = #4898 (dfafd13dce), the parent of PR 4. PR 4 = #4901 (ea94e95a4e), the row-major tail block, the last PR of the four-PR stack. fix = the issue #4934 branch jhan-vnnik-5-i4934 on top of PR 4. An arm named <x>off runs the <x> binary with the kill switch.
the loop, the reader, the dotter

The loop is the software scoring loop of one query against one page. The reader is k_vnni::qk_group, the AVX-512 routine that scores the VNNI blocks of a page. The dotter is the per-token dot product over one row-major K row.

PR 4 keeps an incomplete 16-token K block row-major inside its own bytes and converts it to the VNNI layout at the forward end of the pass that saves its 16th row. The fix runs that conversion on the app pool instead of serially on the main thread.
A cell is one model (qwen-3-4b), tensor-parallel width (tp2 = 2 cards, tp4 = 4 cards), 8 users and a prompt length in tokens; every run generates 256 tokens per user.
TPS is decode throughput, generated tokens per second per user. TTFT is the time to the first token, which here is the prefill time of the whole prompt.

The campaign's threshold for a change: twice the larger sample standard deviation of the two arms over their repetitions, never smaller than 0.40 TPS or 0.15 s. Beyond means the difference is larger than the band.
The mean of the repetition-pair differences divided by their standard error. A large magnitude means the sign is stable across repetitions.
